source_facts: Trading Day is a day on which the relevant Exchange is open for trading.
Trading Day includes a day that would have been open absent a market disruption.
Trading Day excludes days when trading may cease before scheduled Exchange closing time.
Trading Day excludes days with a scheduled shortened period.
Trading Day is defined with respect to an Index Component included in the Index at the Rebalance Day.
Trading Day is defined with respect to every Index Component included in the Index at the Calculation Day immediately following the Rebalance Day.
The provision captures Trading Days for securities to be included as new Index Components.
The securities are included with close of trading on the relevant Exchange on the Rebalance Day.
The Index Administrator is ultimately responsible for whether a day is a Trading Day.
render_facts: A trading day context is valid when it identifies a rebalance day, a day, and an index component.
The context exchange is the component’s relevant exchange.
The component was included in The Index on that rebalance day.
If the day immediately follows that rebalance day, the component was included in The Index on that calculation day.
A valid trading day context is a trading day.
The exchange was open for trading on that day.
A market disruption occurred on that day and the exchange would have been open without the disruption.
There was no trading cessation possibility for that exchange and day before scheduled exchange closing time.
No scheduled shortened period existed for that exchange and day.
A context captures new index component close of trading.
The component is to be included in The Index as a new index component.
The close of trading is for that component’s relevant exchange on that rebalance day.
The Index Administrator is ultimately responsible for any determination whether a valid trading day context is a trading day.
